record.paper_title: Everything You Always Wanted to Know About How Causal Set Theory Can Help with Open Questions in Cosmology, but Were Afraid to Ask
record.original_question: In the Everpresent Lambda model, causal set number-volume fluctuations and a volume-Lambda uncertainty relation yield Lambda approximately proportional to 1 divided by the square root of a spacetime volume V. Which spacetime volume V should be inserted into that relation, such as an observer's past-lightcone volume, and can that choice be justified from causal structure rather than imposed phenomenologically?

evidence.quote: Putting together (6) and (7) we have Λ = ΔΛ ∼ 1/ΔV. Finally substituting the variation of V from (5) we get Λ ∼ 1/√V.

The procedure above still leaves open the question of what volume to insert in (8). A causal choice would be to take the volume of our past lightcone, and this is indeed what is considered in the literature on Everpresent Λ.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Everpresent Λ model arising from causal set theory together with a unimodular-type pairing between the cosmological constant Λ and a spacetime four-volume V. In this framework, the number-to-volume correspondence in a causal set is subject to Poisson fluctuations of size ΔN ∼ √N (equivalently ΔV ∼ √V in fundamental units), and a conjugate volume–Λ uncertainty relation of the form ΔΛ · ΔV ∼ 1 is postulated. Combining these with the assumption that the mean of Λ vanishes (so that Λ ≈ ΔΛ) yields the scaling

   Λ ∼ 1/√V.

The question is: which spacetime four-volume V should appear in this relation? Specifically, give a principled prescription for V (for example, the volume of the past lightcone of a given event, or some other causally defined region), and derive this choice from the causal structure of spacetime as encoded in the underlying causal set, rather than imposing it as a phenomenological input. Provide a justification that explains why the chosen V is the correct conjugate variable to Λ in the fluctuation/uncertainty argument, and analyze the resulting predictions (including correlations of Λ at distinct events) so as to determine whether the prescription is self-consistent within the Everpresent Λ framework.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on Everpresent Λ (e.g., "Aspects of Everpresent Λ (I)", 2023) adopts the past-lightcone volume as the conjugate V used in the fluctuation relation, but treats this as a physically motivated choice rather than one rigorously derived from causal-set causal structure. No derivation establishing this choice from first principles appears in the literature; the question of justifying the volume choice causally remains open.

status_evidence.title: Aspects of Everpresent Λ (I): A Fluctuating Cosmological Constant from Spacetime Discreteness
status_evidence.snippet: Λ stays statistically close to the inverse square root of the spacetime volume; the past lightcone volume is used as V in the model.
status_evidence.claim: Past lightcone volume is the standard choice but is adopted rather than derived from causal structure.

status_evidence.title: Cosmological Tests of Everpresent Λ
status_evidence.snippet: If Λ is determined by Poisson fluctuations of past lightcone volumes, correlations of Λ at two points depend on the intersection of their past lightcones.
status_evidence.claim: Choice of past-lightcone volume is used phenomenologically in tests but not derived from causal structure.
